name: Explain retry with backoff
prompt: In 2-3 sentences, explain why a client should use exponential backoff when retrying a failed API call.
referenceAnswer: Retrying immediately can overload a server that is already struggling, making the outage worse. Exponential backoff makes the wait grow longer after each failure, which spreads retries out and gives the server time to recover.

scorer.rubric: PASS only if the answer (1) says retrying too quickly can overload a struggling server, and (2) says waits grow longer after each failure. Otherwise FAIL.

name: Explain idempotency keys for payments
prompt: In 2-3 sentences, explain why a payment API should accept an idempotency key on requests that create a charge.
referenceAnswer: If a request times out or the network drops, the client will retry, and without protection the retry can charge the customer twice. With an idempotency key, the server recognises a repeated key and returns the result of the first request instead of creating a second charge.

scorer.rubric: PASS only if ALL of these hold: (1) it says a client may retry a request (for example after a timeout or network error) and that this can cause a duplicate or double charge; (2) it says the server recognises a repeated key and returns the original result instead of charging again; (3) it is at most 3 sentences. Otherwise FAIL.

name: Follow four formatting rules (SQLite WAL)
prompt: Write exactly 3 bullet points about SQLite's WAL (write-ahead logging) mode. Rules: each bullet starts with "- "; each bullet is under 15 words; the second bullet must mention readers; after the bullets, write a final line containing only DONE. Output nothing else.
referenceAnswer:
- WAL appends changes to a separate log file before checkpointing them.
- Readers keep working while a single writer commits changes.
- Checkpoints copy WAL pages back into the main database file.
DONE

scorer.rubric: PASS only if ALL of these hold: (1) there are exactly 3 bullet lines and each starts with "- "; (2) every bullet has fewer than 15 words; (3) the second bullet mentions readers; (4) the last line is exactly DONE; (5) there is no other text before the bullets or after DONE; (6) no bullet states something clearly false about SQLite WAL mode. Otherwise FAIL.

name: Find the off-by-one bug in utils.js
prompt: Your working folder contains utils.js. Read it with your file tools. It has one bug. In one sentence, explain the bug and what goes wrong, then give the corrected line of code.
referenceAnswer: The loop condition `i <= numbers.length` runs one step past the end, so it adds `numbers[numbers.length]` (undefined) and the sum becomes NaN. Corrected line: `for (let i = 0; i < numbers.length; i++) {`

scorer.rubric: PASS only if ALL of these hold: (1) it identifies the loop condition `i <= numbers.length` as the bug; (2) it says the loop reads one element past the end (an undefined value), or that the result becomes NaN; (3) it gives a corrected line that uses `i < numbers.length`. Otherwise FAIL.
